subject: science
title: Forces and Magnets
description: How things move on different surfaces, forces that need contact and forces that act at a distance, magnetic materials, and how magnetic poles attract and repel.

objectives.statement: Compare how things move on different surfaces.
Notice that some forces need contact between two objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance.
Observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others.
Compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of whether they are attracted to a magnet, and identify some magnetic materials.
Describe magnets as having two poles.
Predict whether two magnets will attract or repel each other, depending on which poles are facing.

items.prompt: What is the name of the force that slows things down as they slide across a surface?
A toy car is pushed with the same force across different surfaces. On which surface will it roll the furthest?

items.statement: There is more friction on a rough surface than on a smooth one.
A ball rolls more easily on a smooth path than through long grass.

items.prompt: Why is friction useful when you are walking?
items.answer: It stops your feet slipping and helps you grip the ground

items.prompt: Give one example of a force that needs two objects to touch.
Which of these forces can act without the objects touching?

items.statement: A magnet can move a paperclip without touching it.
All forces need two objects to be touching to work.

items.prompt: Name a metal that a magnet will attract.
Which of these objects would a magnet attract?

items.statement: Wood and plastic are not attracted to magnets.

items.prompt: A class tests a coin, a plastic cup, a steel spoon and a rubber band with a magnet. Which will the magnet attract?
How many poles does a magnet have?
items.answer: Two (a north pole and a south pole)

items.prompt: What happens when the north pole of one magnet is held near the north pole of another?
What happens when a north pole is held near a south pole?

items.statement: Two poles that are the same (both north or both south) will repel each other.
Opposite poles of two magnets push away from each other.

items.prompt: Two magnets are pushed together and they spring apart. What does this tell you about the poles facing each other?
items.answer: They are the same poles (both north or both south)
